- If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >95), model often overshoots downward; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per subsequent day.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model fails to adjust; force forecast to align with recent 5-day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.25), model may overreact; cap forecast increase at +3% above prior day’s value to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the window; apply a 1–2% downward bias for first 7 days of forecast.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 3 days, assume model is misaligned with sentiment; reset forecast to 3-day SMA of recent history.
